_what: PROJECT-scope settings for claude-infrastructure. Loaded only when a session's cwd is this repo (or a worktree of it), so nothing here ships to any other project. Deliberately minimal: the operator's ~/.claude/settings.json owns the fleet-wide hooks, deny/ask rules and statusline. This file exists for permissions that are a property of THIS REPO's tooling.
_why_disabledMcpjsonServers: MODE-INDEPENDENT FLOOR for this repo and every worktree of it (backlog eece54939e7f, W3). claude-infrastructure ships no .mcp.json today, so this list blocks nothing right now — that is the point of a floor. A project .mcp.json arrives here the moment anyone copies a reso config into a worktree or writes a probe fixture (the W3 probe itself did exactly that on 2026-08-11), and from then on EVERY headless/`-p`/SDK worker in the directory starts every stdio server in it WITHOUT consulting any approval list (04-spawn-semantics Runs E/E2) — 312 MB per chain for chrome-devtools. Measured 2026-08-11 on 2.1.220: this key, in THIS scope, is the one control that blocks a spawn in that mode (own-process stdio STARTs 1 -> 0 with the http servers still connected), and it is also the ONLY control that reaches an Agent({name}) TEAMMATE, whose launch argv carries no MCP flag for a per-fire flag to ride on. Names, not a wildcard, because the key takes names; these two are the browser servers an infra worktree must never start. Per-fire control for fired sessions: handoff-fire.sh --with-mcp (default is no-inherit).

permissions._why_kitten: scripts/cloud-websetup-drive.sh drives /web-setup by typing into a kitty pane over remote control, and `kitten @ send-text` is the one verb in that flow the auto-mode classifier judges intermittently — the payload is a command line plus a bare `\r`, which reads as an unbounded write to something outside the working tree. Intermittent is the worst shape: the drive gets half-way through an account, blocks on a prompt no one is watching, and the pane is left sitting in /web-setup with consent unanswered. An explicit allow makes the verdict deterministic. The other four verbs are listed for the same reason and because a drive that can type but cannot read the pane back (get-text) is exactly the absence-is-not-success trap the driver exists to avoid.
permissions._why_repo_tooling: MEASURED 2026-08-12 from the manual-approval record, not guessed. The 59 `.claude/settings.local.json` files under ~/Development hold 2,036 DISTINCT approved patterns — 970 of them (48%) exact-match with no wildcard, 359 embedding an absolute path (`Bash(git -C /tmp/wt-accounts-login-cliff rebase origin/main)`). That is the defect: 'yes, don't ask again' writes back a pattern as specific as the invocation that produced it, so it can never match a second time and the same command re-prompts under a new path forever. The entries below are the GENERALIZED prefixes for this repo's own tooling, ranked by live invocation count across 200 recent claude-infrastructure transcripts: bats 366, cc-backlog 237, shellcheck 182, cc-await-ping 160, cc-bats 102, claude-accounts 46, cc-sessions 29, cc-custody 29, wrap-ledger 15. All are query/gate/local-ledger verbs — they read repo state, run the commit gate, or append to an append-only ledger on this box. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, and they must keep prompting: cc-offload / cc-cloud / cc-dispatch (spend Anthropic cloud compute), scripts/deploy-live.sh (mutates the LIVE ~/.claude layer) EXCEPT the two exact converge spellings carved out at the end of the allow list — see _why_converge; the exclusion otherwise STANDS, since that carve-out is exact-match with no `:*` and a prefix pattern cannot wildcard its own middle, so --force, --bootstrap, any other budget value and any other argv all still prompt, and bare `bash:*` / `perl:*` / `node:*` / `awk:*` (arbitrary code execution — `bats:*` is granted instead as the strictly narrower repo gate, and is narrower still than the `python3:*` and `bun:*` the fleet-wide settings.json already grants). Both the bare and `bin/`-prefixed spellings are listed because a prefix pattern cannot wildcard its own middle, and this repo is invoked both ways depending on whether $HOME/.claude/bin is on PATH. `sed -n` and `git fetch` are the two CROSS-REPO entries here, included because `bin/cc-permission-audit` ranks them #1 (2,434 hits) and #6 (382) among commands matching no allow rule fleet-wide; they belong in ~/.claude/settings.json rather than this file, and sit here only so this repo stops paying for them today. CAVEAT on `sed -n`: prefix matching cannot exclude a later flag, so this pattern also admits `sed -n -i …` and sed's `w` write-command. That is a real, narrow widening — accepted because the fleet-wide allow list already grants `python3:*`, `bun:*` and `node -e:*`, each of which is unboundedly wider, and because validate-bash.sh still runs on every call.
permissions._why_converge: THE ONE CARVE-OUT FROM _why_repo_tooling's deploy-live exclusion, granted explicitly by the operator on 2026-09-15 and paired with .claude/CLAUDE.md § Standing-converge authorization. WHAT IT BUYS: `~/.claude` is a per-file symlink farm over this checkout, so a landed commit runs nothing until the shared checkout fast-forwards — and the green-stamp producer emits ~0.17 greens/day against a trunk moving ~63, so T1 is structurally unreachable and every real advance already comes through T2's absence-of-evidence door on a 6h clock. This lets an agent that just landed its own gate-green work converge it now, on that same T2 evidence, instead of waiting out a timer. WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY, and the shape is the safeguard: both entries are EXACT-MATCH with no trailing `:*`, so they admit `CC_DEPLOY_MAX_LAG_COMMITS=0 bash scripts/deploy-live.sh` and NOTHING else — not --force (which takes the tip regardless of RED stamps and bypasses the T1/T1H/T2/T3 ladder outright), not --bootstrap, not another budget value, not one extra flag. Exact-match is normally the defect this file's _why_repo_tooling documents (48% of the fleet's 2,036 approved patterns are exact and therefore never match twice); here it is the point, because the thing being granted is one spelling and the widening is what would be dangerous. WHY A RULE IS NEEDED AT ALL, measured 2026-09-15 as a 2x2, one variable per cell: `bash deploy-live.sh` is ALLOWED for an agent both dry-run and real — it ran twice unattended that day, and the script's own header claiming otherwise was corrected in 00f67bbc7 — while the CC_DEPLOY_MAX_LAG_COMMITS=0 prefix is allowed under --dry-run and DENIED for real. The classifier's rule was never 'agents may not deploy'; it is the narrower and better 'an agent may not alter the gating and then deploy', keyed on the mutation rather than on the env var. This entry is the operator granting that one exception in the open, version-controlled, rather than an agent widening it for itself. RESIDUAL, stated not hidden: a converge carries every sibling commit below the target too, exactly as the timer-driven one does, and it leaves the live tree unstamped until postland-verify catches up — both were already true of T2; what changes is who decides when.
